transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... my wife thought I should come in. It's... mostly just some things going on at work. 

I do mathematical modeling, and... well, on this environmental contract we have right now, I'm pretty sure the people on it are tracking my revisions. They're... they keep planting errors in the datasets. Just to make it look like I can't lead the work. 

My wife, and the junior analysts... they just tell me it's version-control mistakes. But... yeah. I guess that's why I'm here.

When your wife and the junior analysts tell you it's version-control mistakes, do you think there's any possibility they could actually be right about that, or are you completely certain that they're tracking you?

I... no, they're not right. I know what I'm looking at. 

I've been doing this a long time. You don't just... get these kinds of specific errors in the datasets by accident. It's not a version-control thing. They're doing it on purpose. They're tracking what I do and changing it so I look incompetent. I'm... I'm certain.
Besides these concerns about people tracking your work and planting errors, have you been experiencing anything unusual with your senses—like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't see?
No. I... no. Nothing like that. I don't hear voices or... whatever it is you're implying. My senses are perfectly fine.
Outside of work, do you have concerns about other people tracking you or trying to harm your reputation in other areas of your life—like at home, in your personal relationships, or in the community?
No. It's... just at work. It's about the contract, so... no. I don't have issues like that at home, or anywhere else. My personal life is fine.
How long have you been noticing these issues with people planting errors in the datasets and tracking your work revisions?
About... two months. That's when I knew for certain they were doing it. Tracking the revisions and putting those errors in. Just the last two months.

If we were to look at the version-control logs together and they showed these errors were indeed just normal version-control mistakes with no evidence of intentional tampering, would you be able to consider that possibility, or would you still believe people are tracking and planting errors?

No. I wouldn't... it wouldn't change anything. 

My wife already tries to tell me that. Her and the junior analysts... they keep saying it's just version-control mistakes. But I know what I'm looking at. The people on that environmental modeling contract are planting those errors. They're doing it to make it look like I can't lead the work. 

So... no. Whatever the logs say, I know what's happening.

You mentioned they're planting these errors to make you look incompetent and unable to lead the work. Have you thought about why they would specifically want to do that? What do you think their ultimate goal is?
I don't... I don't really know. They just want me off the project. I haven't figured out what they plan to do after that. Just... get me out of the way, I guess. That's all I know.

When you see these errors in the datasets, how do you know for certain that they're specifically trying to make you look bad? Could there be any other explanation for why these errors are appearing, even if you think it's unlikely?

I just... I know. You look at the data and it's obvious. 

I already told you. The people on that environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions. They put the errors right where I'm working so it looks like I can't lead. There isn't any other explanation. I know my wife and the junior analysts keep saying it's just a version-control mistake, but... it's not. 

I don't really have anything else to say about it. That's just what they're doing.

When you look at these errors in the datasets, do you think the people on the contract are deliberately choosing to target you specifically because of something about you personally—like your skills, your position, or something you've done—or do you think this might be happening to other people on the project too?

I don't know about anyone else. I haven't asked them. I just... I just look at my own datasets. 

As for why me specifically... I couldn't tell you. I don't know what it is about me. I just know they're doing it to my work. That's all I know.

When you look at these errors in the datasets, do you think the people on the contract are deliberately putting them there to target you, or could some of these errors just be regular mistakes that happen to show up in your work?

I... I thought I just answered this. They aren't regular mistakes. 

I know my wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just... version-control mistakes, or whatever. But it's not. They are tracking my revisions and planting them there. Deliberately. 

That's... that's why I'm even here talking to you. It's not an accident. I don't really know what else to tell you about it.

When you say they're tracking your revisions and planting errors in the datasets—do you think they're doing this through normal workplace means, like accessing the files directly through the computer system, or do you think there's something else going on that allows them to do this?

I don't... I don't know exactly how they do it. 

I just know they are doing it. They're tracking my revisions. They plant the errors in the datasets so it looks like I can't lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts... they keep saying it's just version-control mistakes. But I know it's not. 

I don't know the exact mechanism. I just know what's happening. That's why I'm here.

When you say they're tracking your revisions and planting errors—do you think they're using technology or surveillance methods that are possible with normal computers and office systems, or do you believe something more unusual or extraordinary is happening to allow them to do this?

I... I already told you. I don't know how they're doing it. 

I just... I'm here because I'm pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions. They're planting errors in the datasets to make it look like I can't lead the work. 

I don't know if it's normal computers or... something else. My wife, the junior analysts... they just say it's version-control mistakes. But I know what's happening. I don't have anything else to say about how they do it.

Besides what's happening at work with the environmental contract, do you find yourself spending a lot of time thinking about this tracking and these planted errors throughout your day—like when you're at home, or doing other things? How much of your time and energy does this take up?

I don't know. I haven't really... kept a log of how much time I spend thinking about it. 

It's just a problem I have to deal with. I don't really know how to quantify the energy it takes up. It's just on my mind sometimes when I'm at home. I don't really have a specific answer for you.

If I asked your wife or the junior analysts about this, and they all insisted they weren't planting errors and weren't tracking your revisions, would any part of you wonder if maybe—even just a little bit—you could be mistaken about what's happening?

No. I wouldn't. 

I know what they'd say. My wife, the junior analysts... they already tell me it's just version-control mistakes. They say it all the time. But... they're wrong. 

I know what's happening. The people on the environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions. They're planting the errors so it looks like I can't lead the work. It doesn't matter what anyone else says about it. I'm not mistaken.
